title: Plato's Bird: name one member of a category, AI vs. people
credit: Human data: Banks, B., & Connell, L. (2023). Category production norms for 117 concrete and abstract categories. Behavior Research Methods, 55(3), 1292-1313. https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-021-01787-z. Data at https://osf.io/jgcu6/, licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

human_data.citation: Banks, B., & Connell, L. (2023). Category production norms for 117 concrete and abstract categories. Behavior Research Methods, 55(3), 1292-1313.
human_data.note: Tables hold aggregate counts of people's first answers (20 UK adults per category) and production frequencies and typicality ratings of the most-named members, normalized by our own rules; no participant-level rows.

ai.spark: muse-spark-1.3, 50 separate calls per category, default sampling, reasoning effort minimal
ai.glimmer: Muse Glimmer 30B (FP8, self-hosted): logit distribution of the first answer token, each top token continued greedily; and 50 samples at temperatures 0.7, 1.0 and 1.5
ai.image: muse-image-1.0, 12 doodles per category (3 calls of n=4)

prompt: Name one member of the category {category}. Answer with one word or a short name only.

glimmer_logits: category hair colour is a broad one

human_named: break any part of the body
metres above and below sea level

human_first: tool you can use to hurt people with
